chip_ctrl.desc: Chip-level control registers (debug, soft reset, blinker, SRAM margins).
chip_ctrl.notes:
First POC2 unit through the unit-first methodology end-to-end.
Phase 1 status:
  spec       -- chip_ctrl_regs.hjson (mirror of dig_msic, pending SSoT migration with Mark)
                + chip_ctrl_intf.yaml (port surface)
  fmod       -- header-only RegisterBlock subclass; hwqe + hw-override paths working
  rtl        -- handwritten wrapper around regtool _reg_top; needs `make spec` to build
  cosim_test -- FMOD-only acceptance test (test_chip_ctrl); RTL lockstep gated on Verilator install
Phase 1 follow-ups:
  - [done] nph_fmod_gen.py auto-generates chip_ctrl_regs.hpp at CMake configure time
  - [done] test_chip_ctrl loads stimulus.json (coroutine driver + BusTxn/BusResp/QeEvent)
  - Coordinate with Mark on SSoT migration (dig_msic chip_ctrl.hjson -> here)
  - Wire poc_arch_eic_as LaTeX to consume gen_macros + gen_register_docs output
  - RTL lockstep (Verilator) gated on -DCHIP_CTRL_RTL=ON

vpu.notes:
T100 diagram name: "VPU -- vector processing unit".
AMOD Phase 8: fmod/src/vpu/spec/vpu_unit.yaml. The only scalar is
simulation_mode (functional, matching OPU default). vpu_num_lanes
lives on SRAM. T100 gap is structural: this class runs opcode
handlers without decoding the VLIW bundle, while vpu_isa/ does.
One of the two terminates the interface; the other is deleted.
Do not build against either until that is settled.

dfe.notes:
T100 diagram name: "DFE -- dataflow engine". The dispatch hub. Inbound it
is an AXI-Lite target whose instruction store the FEP writes; outbound it
masters one port per engine family -- `tdma` to TDMA, `eu` to OVMM/VPU/XPU,
`ucie` to SEND -- and takes results back on `completion`. A `csr` port on
noc_csr carries model-only telemetry (G95: the architecture names a BAR0
page-1 window but places nothing in it).
DfeFmod at src/dfe/{fmod,cosim_test,test} derives from the generated
service loop (src/_gen/from_ssot/dfe_fmod_base.hpp, spec ssot/units/dfe_unit.toml,
arms cmp.cmp, csr.req, cfg_axi.aw, cfg_axi.ar): decode and dispatch by
opcode group in onInput(AW), retirement by cqid with program-order commit
in onInput(CMP), dsync draining, no DFDT resolution yet. In the t100 assembly as
u_dfe, built from config; its connections to u_fep, u_tdma_n, u_xpu and
u_send are declared, not wired (#245). Gaps: G42 (READY vs credit), G43
(HIB as a second requester), G44 (address vs opcode dispatch), G92
(scale_meta overload), G95 (register window without offsets). Legacy
fmod/src/dfe still builds as fmod_dfe pending removal per RFC-INFRA-0003.
Until that removal the legacy class is also Phase 8 config-built from
fmod/src/dfe/spec/dfe_unit.yaml (scalars: simulation_mode = functional,
num_slices must be 1; HBM/SRAM/DMA/VPU/FIFOs stay post-construction).
So one block is described by two specs in two schemas -- the structural
gap to close, and the reason not to clone this class to close it.

ovmm.desc: Optical Vector Matrix Multiply. Kept as ref model for POC2 Phase 1-3.
ovmm.notes:
Port surface refactor planned in Phase 3 to enable config-swap to real OVMM.
AMOD Phase 8: fmod/src/ovmm/spec/ovmm_unit.yaml. Knobs match
OPU::_configure_components() (quantization_bits: 4, not the
compile-time 8). matrix_rows/cols must equal OVMM_MATRIX_*, which are
build-time overrides bounded by what one SRAM line holds
(config/sram_geometry.hpp), not YAML knobs. T100: the monolithic
class covers the whole optical chain. The diagram splits it into
hadamard_enc / ovmm_tx / ovmm_rx / hadamard_dec / accum;
Those five blocks are registered at flavors: [unspecified] -- the split
is on the diagram and nothing is behind it.
Whether the split earns its keep is an open call -- authoring the contract
first is deliberately cheaper than doing the refactor to find out.

sram.notes:
T100 diagram name: "Tensor Memory (TM)"; the spec renamed UTM -> TM.
The most shared interface on the die, and currently a split one: TDMA,
XPU and SEND reach TM over ssot/interfaces/tm_interface.toml (5-channel
AXI), while this model still terminates a single-record port.
Closing that mismatch is what migrating this unit
means.
Gap to M1: geometry is 1024 banks x 64 lines, not 1024 x 1 MiB.

hbm.notes:
T100 diagram name: "HBM4E 0-5 (PHY + MC)"; instantiated six times
(u_hbm4e_0..5). Same split as sram: TDMA and host_dma reach HBM over
ssot/interfaces/hbm_interface.toml, while this model still terminates a
single-record port.
Gap to M1: one generic controller today, not six addressable stacks.
AMOD Phase 8: fmod/src/hbm/spec/hbm_unit.yaml, instance opu_hbm on
t100_amod.yaml (count: 1). Close plan for six stacks:
fmod/doc/HBM_STORE_AND_STACKS.md — one DRAM mmap plus N stack ports
as views, not N heaps. Do not clone HBM into six mmaps. TTB
colocation is not POR; ch 13 §13.1.1 is 8 B across TEs.

dma.desc: AMOD HBM↔SRAM DMA block (legacy fmod DMABlock).
dma.notes:
Not a T100 diagram block. T100 splits DMA into tdma / host_dma /
opu_dma / nic_dma, plus send for the MSIC path. This class is the OPU-internal
HBM↔SRAM mover. Phase 8: fmod/src/dma/spec/dma_unit.yaml.
Instance opu_dma on t100_amod.yaml is this unit, not T100
inter-OPU DMA (see opu_dma below).

opu.notes:
AMOD assembly (not a T100 diagram block). Phase 8 top is
fmod/src/opu/spec/t100_amod.yaml (`--model t100_amod`, AUTOBUILDABLE).
Contract: fmod/doc/AMOD_PHASE8.md.
Loads AUTOBUILDABLE AMOD units as subunits; FIFO datapath stays
setter-wired after construction. Children: sram (opu_sram), hbm
(opu_hbm, count:1), ovmm (opu_ovmm), vpu (opu_vpu), dfe
(opu_dfe), dma (opu_dma). Six T100 stacks are not subunits here —
fmod/doc/HBM_STORE_AND_STACKS.md. T100 OVMM split, VPU VLIW
decode, t100_dfe vs this DFE, and T100 DMA engines vs this
DMABlock are structural, not extra yaml scalars.

pcie_ep.notes:
Phase 2 stub; vendor IP for the actual model.
T100 reuses this unit for all nine PCIe ports -- u_host_pcie,
u_nic_pcie, and u_opu_pcie_0..6. The host / NIC / inter-OPU Gen7 seams have
no SSoT interface spec yet. POC2 stays on Gen3.

msic_bridge.desc: MSIC control/status register projection onto EIC-TX BAR0.
msic_bridge.notes: T100 diagram name: "MSIC interface". Reused on the T100 EIC BAR0.

txa.desc: TX Analog driver array (digital boundary stub for FMOD).
txa.notes: Phase 1: emits one TsvChunk on cosim chain (see _shared/datapath_chain_smoke.hpp).

rxa.desc: RX Analog receiver array (digital boundary stub for FMOD).
rxa.notes: Phase 1: verifies TsvChunk from datapath chain (kPhase1SmokeWord0).

fabio_initiator.notes:
T100 reuses this unit on the MSIC path: SEND -> fabio_initiator ->
serdes -> MSIC. The FABIO contract (common/hw_arch/poc2/intf/fabio.yaml#v1)
is reused unchanged rather than re-declared for T100.
Pairs with MSIC fabio target. Wire model: nph::poc2::fabio::{FabioReq,FabioRsp} single-beat
records per dig_msic fabio_tgt DesignSpec; helpers in _shared/fabio_bus_helper.hpp.
Cosim links with msic_stub (handshake) or msic_fmod (address FABIO).

pic_tx_stub.desc: PIC-TX functional stub at the digital TSV boundary (no optics).
pic_tx_stub.notes: Phase 1: TsvChunk -> FsoChunk pass-through in datapath_chain_smoke.

pic_rx_stub.desc: PIC-RX functional stub at the digital TSV boundary (no optics).
pic_rx_stub.notes: Phase 1: FsoChunk -> TsvChunk pass-through in datapath_chain_smoke.

msic_stub.desc: Placeholder MSIC FMOD until Leick's lands.
msic_stub.notes:
FABIO target stub (Phase 1 single-shot). Same FIFO contract as Leick's MSIC FMOD;
swap is a config/ctor change. metasurface_ctl TBD.

msic.desc: POC2 MSIC FMOD (MsicFmod): FABIO target + OVMM/SRAM-backed matmul compute.
msic.notes:
Blessed as the POC2 MSIC, replacing the msic_stub placeholder in poc2.yaml.
Lives at models/src/msic/fmod/msic_fmod.hpp: addresses the FABIO aperture,
runs the matmul against the OVMM/SRAM oracle, and emits the
`msic.matmul.done` ELOG token that the g4 eic_tx_matmul gate checks.
Same FABIO + register interface as msic_stub (RFC-INFRA-0004); Leick's
production model upstreams to this unit name later.

noc_hs.desc: High-speed custom NoC: bulk tensor traffic between TM and the engines.
noc_hs.notes:
A functional router: correct routing and per-source ordering, no
arbitration delay -- emit the transaction and let PMOD charge for it.
Contention arrives with PMOD P80, charged from the ELOG record.

noc_csr.desc: Arteris low-speed NoC: CSR / BAR access to every block on the die.
noc_csr.notes:
Terminates ssot/interfaces/noc_csr_interface.toml. Transport on CsrTxn
FIFOs: host and SMP initiators, local claim of the 0x01000 window,
forward everything else. Units serve their own csr port with
RegisterFile. libyy AddressMap is the POC2 path, not this one.

The first unit whose spec (ssot/units/noc_csr_unit.toml) is upstream of
BOTH the typed port table it compiles against and the libyy config it
is built from -- so it is also the first with no hand-written Schema D
file. ssot/units/t100_unit.toml is the assembly that instantiates it;
`--config-dir ssot/config --fmod t100` builds the tree. The remaining
T100 units join that assembly one at a time.

pcr.desc: Power / clock / reset domain control to all blocks.
pcr.notes:
Terminates ssot/units/pcr_unit.toml: its own domain_ctl contract plus a
noc_csr target. POC2 chip_ctrl is the closest analog (soft reset, debug)
but covers one chip's registers, not domains.

Built from config in the t100 assembly and connected to nothing, which
is two separate facts: the fabric has one egress and the SMP has it
(t100 gap G36), and no unit yet consumes domain_ctl (pcr gap G35).

xpu.desc: Transpose unit: one tile in from tensor memory, its transpose back out, a completion token to the DFE.
xpu.notes:
ssot::rt::UnitComponent on ssot/units/xpu_unit.toml. Four ports: eu
(target) for dispatch, completion (target, payload outbound) for the
token, tm (initiator) on all five channels, noc_csr (target) for
telemetry. In the t100 assembly as u_xpu, built from config and wired to
nothing -- the DFE is not a subunit here and tensor memory is not a unit
at all.

Work arrives on the eu interface the DFE instantiates as eu_xpu, as three
resolved 64-byte tensor descriptors, and the block decodes one: base (a
tagged pointer whose AST must select UTM), tdims, and dtype.width.
The completion token is Table 4.2.8's three ids and valid bits plus
4.2.8.1's cqid, quoted back exactly as dispatched.

Deleted, not deferred: the geometry CSRs (4.2.5 resolves descriptors in
the DFE, so extents arrive with the work), the signal port (4.2.8 makes
completion DFE-internal), and CTRL.ENABLE. What is left in the RDL is
model-only telemetry, because the architecture defines no XPU registers
at all (G59, asked as T100_arch_spec#69).

Not yet drivable by the DFE end to end: dfe_fmod still fills descriptor
slots with the raw 8-bit index, which this block refuses as a zero extent
rather than transposing (G64, the blocking half of eu G13). The ids and
the cqid do flow correctly.

Gaps: G59 (no architectural register window), G60 (in-place and tile
size), G61 (dtype.width undecodable, supported types unstated), G62
(which operand slot is which), G63 (dims vs tdims), G64 (the DFE sends
indices). Chapter 22 is four empty headings; T100_arch_spec#68 asks for
the dispatch's operand roles.

send.desc: SEND engine: a tile out of tensor memory to the interface its instruction names -- TM again, or MS buffer A or B on the MSIC.
send.notes:
ssot::rt::UnitComponent on ssot/units/send_unit.toml. Five ports: dfe
(ucie, target) for dispatch, cmp (completion, target, payload outbound),
tm (initiator) on all five channels, ms (ms_buf, initiator, write-only)
to the MSIC, csr (noc_csr, target) for telemetry. In the t100 assembly as
u_send, built from config and wired to nothing.

The architecture's fifth dispatch target is SEND -- 4.2.6's five
instruction FIFOs and 4.2.8's five token-returning units. SEND is one-way
from TM to an MS buffer; no instruction defines an MSIC-to-TM direction
or independently strided transfer (G87).

Chapter 5's sequence is what fixes the buffer's shape: two SENDs fill
buffer A, then MSLOADA, then an OVMM with msync. Two tiles before one
load only works if the buffer is addressed, so the model keeps a write
pointer per buffer and test_send case 2 asserts the second tile lands
after the first. Filling from zero instead fails that and nothing else.

Gaps: G87 (no reverse or independently strided MS-buffer transfer), G88
(no architectural register window -- same question as xpu G59,
T100_arch_spec#69), G89 (nothing bounds concurrency, and ch5 makes the
ordering load-bearing), G90 (TSEND and the XPU both transpose TM tiles).
One more is on the interface: ucie G84, whether a SEND sets a DFRT ready
bit at all. 4.2.3 says its completion info carries a destination
descriptor, but chapter 3's SEND and TSEND layouts have no dst field and
the AST nibble has no code for MSIC SRAM, so a descriptor cannot name an
MS buffer. Token goes back with dstv clear, which is the side chapter 3
supports; T100_arch_spec#70 asks 4.2.3 to be corrected.

hadamard_enc.desc: Hadamard encode: rotates an activation tile before the modulators.
hadamard_enc.notes: First hop of the optical chain. Inside the OVMM monolith today.

ovmm_tx.desc: Optical TX: lane mapping and modulator drive toward the APIC.
ovmm_tx.notes: Maps encoded symbols onto lanes and drives the modulators.

ovmm_rx.desc: Optical RX: capture and digitise. Block scaling is proposed here, not implemented.
ovmm_rx.notes:
Captures and digitises the optical product. Vanilla T100 applies no
scaling in the RX at all -- the OVMM is int4 x int4 -> int32 and the
descriptor's dtype.scaled is clear. Block scaling is a proposal, and this
is where it would land if it lands anywhere: per-block scales apply to
partial sums before accumulation collapses them, so at block_size 16 and
K 1024 one dispatch carries 65,536 partials (256 KiB) against 1,024
collapsed outputs (4 KiB), a 64x amplification that rules out a VPU
kernel. fmod/src/scale_engine/ implements the arithmetic as an
experiment, reachable only from the legacy host-pointer driver and not
from any DFE program. The previous description -- "apply block scales",
present tense -- read as a commitment and led to block scaling being
treated as settled hardware (models#303); it is intent.

hadamard_dec.desc: Hadamard decode: inverse transform of the captured product.
hadamard_dec.notes: Inverse transform, producing INT32 partial products for one K step.

accum.desc: Accumulators: INT32 ping-pong accumulation across K.
accum.notes:
Ping-pong INT32 accumulation across K, then one tile back to TM. Inside
ovmm performGEMM today. When this is modelled: k_total on the outgoing
tile is the completeness check -- a tile written with fewer K steps than
the command asked for is a silent wrong answer.

hti.desc: Host interface block (HIB): host-memory SQ/CQ rings, region admission, the fence bank.
hti.notes:
T100 diagram name: "HIB". Terminates ssot/units/hti_unit.toml: an
axi4_lite target for BAR0 MMIO and an axi4_full initiator to host
memory, plus region_admit to the FEP, dma, and noc_csr both ways.

Having a port that reaches host memory is what made ch11 modellable
here. The SQ fetch and the CQE write are real bursts, so the register
staging and the one-deep CQ_LAST ring the previous model used as
stand-ins are deleted rather than migrated (models#247). Register
offsets mirror the vendored ssot/isa/t100_bar0.rdl at the
architecture's own addresses, hole included.

fep.desc: Front-end processor: takes a region from the HIB, walks its command buffer, masters the DFE ingress.
fep.notes:
Terminates ssot/units/fep_unit.toml: region_admit as target, axi4_lite
as initiator into the DFE. It receives a region tuple and an interrupt,
not a queue entry -- ch2 2.3.2 and ch11 11.1.2 (models#248 assumed
otherwise and was closed).

No credit accounting: ch4 4.2.2 has the DFE deassert READY when its
instruction FIFO fills, so a write can be made to wait but not dropped,
and a bounded fifo does that unaided (models#247). DFE_STALLS is the
diagnostic that replaced the credit register. QEMU cosim-direct remains
the shortcut to real firmware behavior rather than modelling the CPU.

smp.desc: System management processor (RISC-V): redundancy, calibration, telemetry.
smp.notes:
Serves ssot/interfaces/noc_csr_interface.toml as both a target (BAR0
0x29000) and a CSR initiator (reads/writes other units over Arteris).
Housekeeping only: it reaches every block through the CSR fabric, never
through the datapath, and calibration is a CSR write rather than a
CalUpdate sidecar.

rot.desc: Root of trust: secure boot, attestation, OTP reads.
rot.notes:
Secure boot and attestation: fetch firmware over QSPI, measure it, read
fuses, then release the boot sequencer.

boot_seq.desc: Boot sequence controller: orders domain bring-up and firmware fetch.
boot_seq.notes: Orders domain bring-up and per-block release once the RoT is satisfied.

tdma.desc: Tensor DMA: HBM4E <-> TM transfer, plus MZERO and DSTORE. Instantiated as TDMA N and TDMA S.
tdma.notes:
ssot::rt::UnitComponent on ssot/units/tdma_unit.toml. Five ports: dfe
(target, the tdma interface the DFE already instantiates), cmp
(completion, target, payload outbound), hbm and tm both initiator on all
five channels, csr (noc_csr, target) for telemetry. In the t100 assembly
as u_tdma_n only, built from config and wired to nothing.

The one rule this block has to get right is 4.2.8: a write's completion
token means the bytes are globally visible, so it follows the hbm port's
`b` and not its last `w` beat. test_tdma case 2 asserts the distinction
causally. Work arrives only on the `tdma` dispatch port with descriptors
resolved by the DFE; the model emits real AXI-shaped bursts on both
memories and returns cqid plus descriptor ids on completion.

u_tdma_n serves HBM4E 0-2 and u_tdma_s 3-5, carried as stack_first /
stack_count and range-checked per dispatch. u_tdma_s is NOT in the
assembly: a unit instantiated twice with different parameters cannot be
expressed yet (t100 G73, models#255), and writing it would build a second
north engine under a southern name.

Gaps: G66 (blocking -- DLOAD has nowhere to deliver its descriptor, since
the DFDT's one write port is spent on TADVANCE), G67 (strided vs
contiguous is undecidable on this port), G68 (ch21 is five empty
headings), G69 (no field states a transfer length), G70 (AST vs opcode
direction), G71 (nothing bounds concurrency), G72 (a flat HBM offset with
no stack field, against a port that requires one).

host_dma.desc: HOST DMA: host system memory <-> HBM, driven from an SQ entry. Chapter 11's `HOST` engine.
host_dma.notes:
ssot::rt::UnitComponent on ssot/units/host_dma_unit.toml. Four ports:
xfer (dma, target -- the far end of u_hti's `dma` port), host (axi4_full,
initiator, EXTERNAL, 64-bit beats), hbm (initiator, all five channels),
csr (noc_csr, target) for telemetry. In the t100 assembly as u_host_dma,
built from config and wired to nothing. Not a DFE client: 4.2.8's list of
units returning completion tokens does not include it.

Two things are load-bearing. 11.3.2 -- a completion is
signalled "only once the transferred bytes are visible in HBM to every
other agent" -- so the completion follows the hbm port's `b`, and
test_host_dma case 1 asserts it causally. Chapter 11's AXI requester is
the external `host` port, so bursts, responses, and performance traffic
are visible at the unit boundary.

11.3.1 gives each controller its own staging SRAM, so a transfer is two
hops rather than one copy, chopped at stage_bytes and counted in HOPS. No
chapter sizes that buffer (G77); 4096 is one RFC-T100-0005 placement
quantum, so a hop cannot straddle two HBM frames.

Half the transfer descriptor is not a transfer this engine performs.
Chapter 11 rules layout out of the transport command twice, so rank, dims
and both stride vectors are refused and counted (dma G74) rather than
executed. The stack is decoded from the device address as TDMA decodes
it (G79), rather than configured through a separate STACK_CFG. Its
register map is entirely model-only: Table 11-2 names BAR0 page 2 and
never populates it (G75).

opu_dma.desc: Inter-OPU DMA: HBM <-> remote HBM across the seven OPU PCIe ports.
opu_dma.notes:
DmaEngine::DMA2/DMA3 are enums only today. When this is specified: the
remote endpoint is an address space, not a separate interface, which is
why one descriptor shape covers local and remote transfers.

nic_dma.desc: NIC DMA: NIC <-> HBM for the host network stack.
nic_dma.notes:
Moves packet chunks between the crypto block and HBM. Not on the compute
path. DmaEngine::NET0 is an enum only.

serdes.desc: 40-80 lane SERDES at 112 Gb/s (PHY + PCS/FEC) to the MSIC.
serdes.notes:
Bonds lanes and carries FABIO beats to the MSIC. Lane count is config --
a block must not assume 40 or 80 -- and FEC is a status flag, not coding.
txa/rxa are the only existing analogs and they are POC2 digital-boundary
stubs, not SERDES.

nic_bridge.desc: NIC bridge: host <-> NIC PCIe forwarding.
nic_bridge.notes:
Pure forwarding of host PCIe transactions to the NIC port and back: no
packet awareness, which is the crypto and DMA blocks' job.

nic_crypto.notes:
FMOD models key-context lookup and framing, not the cipher -- the payload
passes through marked processed, because an actually-encrypting model
makes golden vector comparison harder for no functional gain.

uart.notes: RoT console, one byte at a time, bridged to the host-side console.

qspi.desc: QSPI flash controller for firmware image fetch.
qspi.notes: Serves firmware image reads to the RoT from external flash.

otp.desc: One-time-programmable fuse array with lock bits.
otp.notes: Fuse array with lock bits. A locked row returns zero, not an error.

apic_stub.desc: APIC optical interconnect, functional pass-through (no optical physics).
apic_stub.notes:
Off-die. Modelled exactly as POC2 models FSO: the frame arrives intact
and in order. No loss, no crosstalk, no calibration -- if a test needs
those it injects them, the model never invents them. No CSR port:
nothing on the EIC configures it.

ms_dma.why: Replaced by SEND, the engine chapter 4 actually names, dispatched on the DFE's ucie port. Not a pure rename -- SEND is the specified block and ms_dma was the placeholder for it -- so the tile_in_tm and pevents_emitted obligations moved across rather than being dropped.

ladder.name: t100_fmod_ladder
ladder.desc: Capability milestones for the T100 functional model, in dependency order.

backends.label: runtime + mock
backends.desc: A device emulator with no model behind it. Proves the runtime's seam -- submission, completion, error paths -- and deliberately proves nothing about the machine. Green here is necessary and never sufficient.

backends.label: runtime + intrinsics
backends.desc: Real arithmetic, no timing and no unit structure: the operation is computed directly instead of being walked through the model. This is the row that answers "is the gate test written?", because a contract test can run here long before the FMOD can execute it.

backends.label: runtime + AMOD
backends.desc: The OPU assembly -- SRAM, HBM, OVMM, VPU, DFE, DMA as real components on a scheduler. A functional model, not a shortcut, which is why it and not intrinsics is the bar a gate has to clear. Note the backend hand-builds OPU rather than loading fmod/src/opu/spec/t100_amod.yaml through ConfigDB, so today this row is "the AMOD" only by convention.

backends.label: runtime + T100 FMOD
backends.desc: The assembly in t100.yaml -- the chip this program is actually building. No backend stands it up yet, so the row is empty by construction rather than for want of tests. That emptiness is the most load-bearing thing on this chart: every green square above it was earned on a different assembly.

fidelities.label: Functional model
fidelities.desc: The C++ FMOD assembly. Proves the program is right and the units agree on their contracts. Says nothing about timing, gate-level behaviour, or anything the RTL adds -- which is exactly why it is the floor and not the ceiling.

fidelities.label: RTL / cosim
fidelities.desc: The synthesisable RTL under a cosim testbench (UVM/Xcelium), driven by the same vectors. The first fidelity that can disagree with the FMOD for a hardware reason. Evidence is a ctest the cosim lane registers.

fidelities.label: Emulation / FPGA
fidelities.desc: The design on emulation or an FPGA board. Does not run under ctest, so its evidence is a machine-readable run record (board/bitstream/seed/result), not a JUnit case.

fidelities.label: Silicon
fidelities.desc: The part. The only fidelity that settles it, and the one that must never be hand-marked green: evidence is a run-record artifact (stepping, firmware and runtime SHA, vector id, counters) fed through the same scorer.

waves.name: Plumbing
waves.desc: Every unit instantiable and addressable, and the chip top standing up from config. Mostly register and link work, which makes it the most parallel block on the ladder -- units barely touch each other here.

waves.name: First GEMM
waves.desc: A tile reaches Tensor Memory and a matmul agrees with an oracle. The first point at which the model computes something a person recognises.

waves.name: Real datapath
waves.desc: The DFE drives the engines and the VPU chains ops, with no test harness standing in for the hardware and no back doors left in the model.

waves.name: Whole model
waves.desc: Layer, token, batch, and a timing number we are willing to quote to someone outside the team. One real network end to end.

waves.name: Model coverage
waves.desc: The architectures a customer will actually ask about, which is where routing and cache pressure stop being someone else's problem. Dated well past the others on purpose: nothing here is credible until W4 lands.

milestones.label: Out of reset
milestones.proves: The unit builds from config, releases reset, and runs to idle without error. Asserts almost nothing on purpose: it is the proof that a second test has somewhere to live.

milestones.label: Registers respond
milestones.proves: CSR reads return the reset values the register SSoT declares, and writes obey its access policy (round-trip for writable state, ignored for hardware-owned state, error for an unmapped address).

milestones.label: Moves a payload
milestones.proves: A transport unit accepts a transaction on one side and the same bytes arrive on the far side, in order. The rung for units whose whole job is carriage rather than compute.

milestones.label: Host<->HBM (super-unit)
milestones.proves: Two ordered SQ DMA commands move a host buffer to HBM and back to a DIFFERENT host address through the assembled hti + host_dma + hbm split units, and every byte survives. No PCIe endpoint, no fabric, no compute: the smallest thing that exercises the ring, the doorbell, the staging hop and the HBM slab on the real block boundaries.

tests.note: The gate: the real HtiFmod and HostDmaFmod wired together with host and HBM memory models, replaying the shared vector host -> HBM -> a DIFFERENT host address as real bursts across the block boundaries (SQ ring, doorbell, the XFER/DONE handoff, host_dma's staging hops, the HBM slab). Built by fmod/integration/host_hbm_su and registered as the ctest below. Promote up `evidence:` as the same vector replays on RTL, FPGA and silicon.

Functional evidence: the SAME vector replayed through the runtime SQ DMA path on fmod:// (contract 20). runtime_amod topology, so it is informational and cannot close the rung -- the split-units test above is the gate. This is what makes the vector and its byte-identity oracle real before the assembly exists, and it exercises the ring, the doorbell, the DMA engines and the HBM slab on the AMOD.

milestones.label: Host DMA round-trip (chip)
milestones.proves: A host buffer DMAs to HBM and back in one ordered batch through the assembled top -- pcie_ep, the ring, the doorbell, the completion path and the HBM slab -- and every byte survives, with no compute anywhere.

tests.note: The host_hbm_su vector, replayed through the assembled top so pcie_ep is in the path rather than bypassed. Waits on the chip top (there is no src/eic yet; src/eic_tx is the pattern).

INFORMATIONAL, not gating. One binary registered against every backend and green on the AMOD, so it proves the ring/doorbell/HBM logic is functionally right -- but the runtime's fmod backend enters at a monolithic hti that copies host<->HBM internally, bypassing the split host_dma block and pcie_ep entirely. Real functional evidence, wrong topology to close a target-hardware rung, so `target_topology: chip_top` keeps it off the gate. See host_hbm_su for the split-unit proof.

milestones.label: Chip bring-up
milestones.proves: The whole T100 EIC top builds from t100.yaml, comes out of reset, and answers a BAR0 walk with the block-presence sentinel of every unit behind it. Boots far enough to prove the address map, not far enough to compute anything.

tests.note: Pattern exists one chip over: src/eic_tx/cosim_test/ test_eic_tx_autobuild.cpp already builds a chip top from config and drives host BAR0 MMIO through a fabric AddressMap. This is that test with t100.yaml's unit list.
Reads the ID register of every unit in t100.yaml at its BAR0 offset. Cheap, and it is the test that catches an address map that drifted from the manifest.

milestones.label: Secure boot completes
milestones.proves: RoT reads its fuses from OTP, fetches a firmware image over QSPI, verifies it, and releases the boot sequencer, which brings the clock and reset domains up in the order the spec declares. The chip is trusted and powered before anyone asks it to compute.

tests.note: Drives the whole chain rather than each link: a deliberately corrupted image must fail to release boot_seq, which is the only assertion that proves verification is load-bearing and not decorative.

milestones.label: HBM<->TM (super-unit)
milestones.proves: A minimum legal TDMA descriptor moves one line HBM->TM and TM->HBM through the assembled hbm + tdma + sram units and the bytes match an oracle, with completion signalled only after the transfer is visible. No DFE, no compute.

tests.note: The gate: the real TdmaFmod wired to HBM and TM memory models, replaying the shared vector HBM -> TM -> a DIFFERENT HBM address as real bursts across the interface::hbm and interface::tm boundaries (MREAD then MWRITE, a minimum-legal [N,1] 1-byte-element tile). No FEP, no DFE, no KICK -- TDMA is driven directly, the TM analogue of host_hbm_su. Built by fmod/integration/tm_hbm_su. Promote up `evidence:` as the same vector replays on RTL, FPGA and silicon.

milestones.label: TM via DFE KICK (super-unit)
milestones.proves: A command buffer of DLOAD x3, MREAD, MWRITE moves a tile HBM->TM->HBM, dispatched by the DFE from a real FEP KICK with no back door, and the DFE refuses MZERO terminally so the decoder advertises what it supports.

tests.note: Reuses the focused DLOAD/MREAD/MWRITE logic of runtime/tests/contract/08_dfe_fmod.cpp, but on the assembled split units driven by the FEP block rather than the runtime's region executor. Blocked on real DLOAD descriptor resolution in the DFE.

milestones.label: TM round-trip (chip)
milestones.gpu: upload and read back a texture
milestones.proves: Host bytes reach HBM, cross into Tensor Memory and come back byte-identical on the assembled top, driven by a real DFE command buffer rather than a back door. Still no arithmetic: the whole data plane working, compute idle.

tests.note: The tm_dfe_su vector replayed through the assembled top. Waits on the chip top.

INFORMATIONAL, not gating. Green on the AMOD: assembles DLOAD x3, MREAD, MWRITE, asserts byte identity, and asserts MZERO faults terminally. Real functional evidence, but on the runtime's hand-built OPU rather than the t100.yaml top, so `target_topology: chip_top` keeps it off the gate. See tm_dfe_su for the split-unit proof.

milestones.label: FEP alive, one NOP (super-unit)
milestones.proves: A preloaded one-word NOP command buffer in HBM is fetched by the FEP on a directly injected KICK, the DFE retires the NOP locally, and the FEP reports OK -- on the assembled hbm + fep + dfe units with no host stack in the path.

tests.note: Direct KICK into hbm + fep + dfe, no HTI. The firmware ABI half is already unit-tested in fep_fw/tests/test_default_fep.cpp; this rung is the assembled command-buffer contract. Treat G47 in ssot/units/fep_unit.toml as blocking for hardware-faithful promotion: the FEP needs a real HBM read port here, not the address-as-word stand-in.

milestones.label: Host KICK -> CQE (super-unit)
milestones.proves: A command buffer is DMA'd to HBM, a KICK is submitted through the SQ, the FEP walks it and the DFE retires it, and the correlated terminal CQE comes back -- through the assembled hti + host_dma + hbm + fep + dfe units.

tests.note: The fep_nop_alive buffer, now delivered over the host path and reaped as a CQE. Unwritten in this tree.

milestones.label: Firmware runs
milestones.proves: FEP walks a command buffer out of HBM and stores DFE instructions, and SMP runs a calibration pass and a telemetry loop over the CSR fabric. The two embedded CPUs are executing their own code rather than being poked by a test harness.

tests.note: FEP already has a cosim_test and the notes point at QEMU cosim-direct rather than modelling the core, so this rung is about the command-buffer contract, not about an instruction-set model.
SMP is the second initiator on the CSR fabric, so its calibration writes are also the test that the fabric tolerates two masters.

milestones.label: One tile in TM
milestones.proves: A strided transfer lands a tile in Tensor Memory, and completion is observable only after the write is visible.

milestones.label: DFE dispatches one op
milestones.proves: A single op arrives at its engine as an engine_bus command from the dataflow engine rather than from a test harness holding the wires, and reports completion. Says nothing about whether the result is correct.

tests.note: Split out of the whole-binary contract so a rung can name a capability rather than a file. This one is the smallest claim the rung makes: a kernel was reached through a real KICK, decoded its operands and moved bytes. Green on both backends: `T100RT_Op_abi_fmod` is the AMOD sibling, because OpuEngineBus now dispatches VCALL through the same kernel ABI. The rung still waits on ovmm_dispatch (G-17) and on XPU, which still fault.

The case the backend rows exist to make legible. Written and green on intrinsics://, where OVMM is an fp32_passthrough of the descriptor extents. Absent from the AMOD column on purpose: both backends now read the descriptor dims, but fmod:// OVMM is [N, K] nibble lines, m=1, 4-bit optical, while this contract's operands are the intrinsics:// [K, N] int8 fp32_passthrough (G-17). Registering T100RT_Op_ovmm_fmod would claim a pass the machine cannot give. VCALL is no longer the reason this cell is empty -- XPU, SEND and MZERO still terminate.

milestones.label: One GEMM vs oracle
milestones.proves: A matmul agrees bit-exactly with a reference implementation, driven through the optical chain rather than called directly.

tests.note: The fp32 half, and it exists: a hand-checked 2x3x2 through a real KICK plus the shape matrix, on intrinsics. It is not the rung's "bit-exactly" claim -- fp32_passthrough at 1e-6 is a tolerance -- so it cannot close this gate alone, which is why the int4 entry below stays open. Two entries is the mechanism that stops a half-built oracle showing green. Runs on the AMOD, so with target_topology: chip_top it is functional evidence, not a gate closer.

The oracle is the cheap part -- a NumPy matmul at the model's quantisation. The work is driving the chain without back doors. Oracle comparisons already exist one level down in fmod/testbench/ovmm/ and fmod/integration/eic_tx_matmul/; what is missing is one at chip level through the DFE.

The chip_top gating slot: the int4-vs-oracle GEMM through the assembled optical chain on the t100.yaml top, asserting operands are resident in TM/HBM (not host-staged) before the KICK. Unwritten; this is what closes the rung rather than the AMOD entries above.

milestones.label: Program a metasurface tile (super-unit)
milestones.proves: A minimum legal weight tile moves TM -> SEND -> metasurface buffer, SEND completion means the bytes are visible, and a second SEND appends rather than overwrites -- on assembled dfe + sram + send + msic.

tests.note: Reuses src/send/cosim_test/test_send.cpp stimulus. The three ordered seams (TM->SEND move, SEND-writes-buffer-visible, second-SEND-appends) are the ones the plan lists; each is a check inside this test.

milestones.label: One OVMM vs oracle (super-unit)
milestones.proves: MSLOADA/B programs a tile and msync blocks OVMM until settle; OVMM consumes one activation tile and one programmed weight tile; accum writes one result tile to TM, compared exactly against an integer/quantised reference. Optical tolerance belongs to a separate named RNM fidelity gate, not here.

tests.note: BLOCKED: MSLOADA/MSLOADB has no row in ssot/isa/dfe_isa.toml, so the program this test would assemble cannot be expressed. The oracle is the cheap part (a NumPy matmul at the tile's quantisation); the work is the missing ISA/control seam. Do not close this by calling the OVMM model directly -- that would prove the optics, not the datapath.

milestones.label: Every VPU instruction (super-unit)
milestones.proves: Every mnemonic in the VPU ISA SSoT has a semantic oracle vector that replays on assembled sram + vpu + dfe + fep, executed in increasing machinery (scalar/NOP, load/store/move, integer ALU/loops, vector moves, basic FP, reciprocal/divide/sqrt, reductions/top-k, transcendental/ activation). Strict census parity: a TOML row with no case fails the gate.

tests.note: The census itself (every TOML mnemonic has a semantic case) is enforced today by scripts/tests/test_vpu_isa_census.py against fmod/src/vpu/test/plan.yaml (the census SSoT), with the standalone semantic layer in vpu_isa/tests/test_vpu.cpp. This rung is the assembled replay of those vectors through a real KICK, which is unwritten in this tree.

milestones.label: VPU op chain
milestones.proves: Quantise, GEMM and dequantise run as one chain with no back-door calls.

tests.note: add, mul, SiLU, GELU and their fail-closed cases, as VCALL kernels through a real KICK. Green on both backends (`T100RT_Op_vpu_fmod`). The rung still waits on the quantise/dequantise pair below. AMOD topology, so functional evidence rather than a gate closer.

Nearest existing thing is runtime/tests/contract/11_dfe_persistent.cpp, which runs GEMM plus an RMSNorm VCALL against persistent HBM weights. RMSNorm would now dispatch on fmod://; the GEMM half would not (G-17). The chain this rung is named for is still missing, and contract 11 is not registered on the AMOD for that reason.

The chip_top gating slot: quantise -> GEMM -> dequantise/residual as one chain on the assembled top, with no host intermediate between the stages (intermediates stay resident in TM). Unwritten; this closes the rung rather than the AMOD VCALL entries above.

milestones.label: P-events emitted
milestones.proves: The unit fires its declared timing events at the right seams, each naming the component that emitted it. PMOD attaches cost to these seams, so an emit that silently disappears is a hole in the timing model that no functional test would notice.

milestones.label: One layer
milestones.proves: A whole decoder block: norm, attention, feed-forward, residual.

tests.note: The AMOD layer contract. Functional evidence; with target_topology: chip_top it does not close the rung on its own.

The chip_top gating slot: norm, attention, feed-forward and residual as one decoder block on the assembled top, with activations and the KV update resident in TM/HBM rather than staged through the host. Unwritten.

milestones.label: One token (Llama-2-7B)
milestones.proves: A full forward pass emits one token that matches the reference implementation. Dense and small on purpose: the first end-to-end run should fail for one reason at a time.

tests.note: Phoebe serves llama-7b-nph (meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf) today, and phoebe/tests/test_fmod_pipeline.py already generates tokens through the FMOD bridge -- but on _tiny_llama() factories, d_model <= 128 and untrained weights. So the plumbing is proved and the claim is not: this rung is that test on a real checkpoint.

milestones.label: PMOD gets data
milestones.proves: Enough of the model runs, with enough seams emitting, that PMOD produces an end-to-end timing number for a real workload. Whether that number is trustworthy is PMOD's question and PMOD's ladder; this rung is the point at which they can start asking it.

milestones.label: Many tokens (dense)
milestones.proves: Batched decode with a KV cache, across the four dense configs in lmod/tests/test_configs.yaml. Coverage rather than new capability: the shapes change, the datapath does not. The five DeepSeek configs in that same file wait on moe_routing, which is what splits the nine.

tests.note: The four dense configs replayed on the assembled top, with weights and the KV cache resident in HBM/TM. Numerical parity alone does not close it: the trace must show no per-token host round-trip.

milestones.label: One MoE block (synthetic)
milestones.proves: A sparse block computes what the dense reference computes: the router picks k experts per token, each selected expert's MLP runs, and the weighted combine reassembles the rows in token order. Synthetic weights and a handful of experts on purpose -- this rung is about the dispatch being faithful to whatever the router decides, not about what a trained router decides, so it fails for one reason at a time.

tests.note:
Unwritten in this repo, and the capability is nevertheless proved today -- which is the distinction this ladder's backend columns exist to keep. phoebe#84 runs a synthetic Mixtral block on intrinsics:// with the router GEMM, softmax, expert SwiGLU, weighted scale and combine all on the device, matching PyTorch's logits; see phoebe/tests/test_session_moe.py. AMOD topology, so functional evidence -- the chip_top entry below is what closes the rung.
The measurement that rung produced is the load-bearing part, and it is on models#401: 34-43% of the block's regions exist only to move rows into per-expert order and back, MREAD/MWRITE outnumber OVMM 14-16 to one, and the permutation cost is linear in rows dispatched (~2.5 regions per row) rather than per bucket. Extrapolated to DeepSeek-V3 at prefill batch that is ~1.25M regions per MoE layer against ~512 for a bucket-granular primitive. Routing is therefore movement-bound.
UPDATE (FEP routing path): those permutation regions are the reason the FMOD backends now install the FEP routing personality (T100_CAP_FEP_MOE_ROUTE_V1, FepRegionExecutor -- see backend_fmod.cpp and contract/01_hello.c). The row gather/scatter into per-expert order is now the FEP's job on-device, not ~1.25M host-emitted regions. That moves the movement cost off the host command path onto the FEP, so the chip_top gate below must assert the permutation regions originate in the FEP (device), not the host -- otherwise the on-device routing win is invisible and a host-emitted permutation could pass on parity alone.

The chip_top gating slot: a synthetic MoE block on the assembled top where the router picks k experts, each selected expert's MLP runs, and the weighted combine reassembles rows in token order -- with the row permutation emitted by the FEP routing personality, asserted from the region source, not the host. Unwritten.

milestones.label: MoE (DeepSeek-V3-16B)
milestones.proves: A mixture-of-experts decode: the router picks experts per token, and only the chosen expert weights are streamed. The first workload where memory traffic depends on the data, which is what makes it the interesting one for PMOD. Smallest DeepSeek first, so the routing is the only new thing.

tests.note:
The routing-semantics dependency is closed and the serving one is not. phoebe#84 executes a real top-k and dispatches exactly the experts it selects, so expert selection is exact and traffic that depends on which experts fire can be validated (moe_block). With the FEP routing personality now advertised on the FMOD backends (T100_CAP_FEP_MOE_ROUTE_V1), the per-token expert gather/scatter is an on-device FEP step rather than a host-emitted region stream, so this rung's gate must assert that only the chosen expert weights are streamed AND that the routing permutation originates in the FEP. What blocks this rung is no longer routing but DeepSeek itself.
That remaining dependency is entirely in Phoebe and has two parts, both needed before there is anything to serve. DeepSeek-V3 is modelled in phoebe/src/phoebe/logical_tracer.py (DeepSeekArch: MLA attention, dense-then-MoE FFN) and in the Excel/LLIR path, but is absent from Phoebe's MODEL_REGISTRY. And its class names have to reach the hook allowlists: a patched Mixtral today reports Attention 0 and RMSNorm 0, because MixtralRMSNorm and MixtralAttention are in neither SESSION_RMSNORM_TYPES nor SESSION_ATTENTION_TYPES -- so an MoE model gets less of itself onto the device than a Llama does, and DeepSeek's own classes will land in the same hole.

milestones.label: Scale (405B / 671B)
milestones.proves: The big end of the config set. Weights and KV cache both stop fitting anywhere convenient, so this is the rung where staging from HBM has to happen without stalling the pipe. Analysed today in the Excel/LLIR path and in logical-tracer parity tests (test_llama_405b_prefill_matches_lmod); never executed as inference. Completing this rung and moe_routing together accounts for all nine configs plus 405B.

tests.note: The big configs on the assembled top, where weights and KV cache both spill HBM. The gate must assert staging from HBM proceeds without stalling the pipe and without a host round-trip per stage -- residency and traffic, not just token parity.

workstreams.label: Gate tests
workstreams.desc: The integration tests named in every rung's gate: block. Three of them are written and two of those pass outright, all three living in runtime/tests/contract/ rather than in src/*/cosim_test/ -- which is where this ladder went looking for them and why it reported nothing reached for longer than it should have. The rest are unwritten and the row is unowned. Until someone owns it, a chip rung cannot be claimed no matter how many unit squares fill in.

workstreams.label: Chip top
workstreams.desc: There is no src/eic. Every chip-level rung that needs the assembled top needs a build of the t100.yaml unit list behind a fabric AddressMap, and it does not exist -- src/eic_tx is the pattern to copy. Eleven of nineteen rungs sit behind it, which makes it the largest unowned dependency here. Not all of them, though, and that is the useful part: host_loopback, tm_roundtrip and dfe_dispatch are already reachable through the runtime's own fmod backend without any chip top at all.

workstreams.label: Test harness
workstreams.desc: Per-case doctest reporting, the CMake plumbing that discovers src/<unit>/test, plan.yaml parity checking and the milestone rollup. Landed in models #215 and #216; listed because the unit rungs assume it and because it is the one row that is actually finished.

workstreams.label: Phoebe stack
workstreams.desc:
Outside the models repo and outside modelling's control, which is exactly why it belongs on the chart -- and, as of the runtime cutover, the place most of these rungs are reached first rather than last. See bringup_strategy below for why that ordering is deliberate and what the FMOD is expected to inherit from it.
Reached on intrinsics:// today: a whole decoder block including its residual additions (phoebe#83), attention with its operands resident and a device KV cache (phoebe#85), and a synthetic MoE block (phoebe#84). Two gaps remain, both narrower than they were. DeepSeek-V3 is modelled in the logical tracer but absent from Phoebe's MODEL_REGISTRY -- and the Mixtral work makes clear that the allowlists (SESSION_RMSNORM_TYPES, SESSION_ATTENTION_TYPES) will need its class names too, or the model runs with less of itself on the device than a Llama does. And every end-to-end generate test runs on tiny synthetic weights rather than a real checkpoint, which is the one that keeps one_token honest: parity on d_model 32 is not parity on 4096.

open_questions.question: The metasurface-programming instructions MSLOADA and MSLOADB are described in prose in the DFE chapter but have NO row in ssot/isa/dfe_isa.toml. There is no opcode, so there is no instruction an assembler can emit, a DFE can decode, or a test can drive -- which is why ovmm_one_su is marked blocked rather than given a gate test that would have to reach around the ISA. What is the encoding: two opcodes or one with a bank select, what operands (tile descriptor, bank, settle/msync semantics), and does msync become its own instruction or a field? Until this is settled the entire metasurface/OVMM datapath (rung 4) cannot be exercised through the real control path, only by calling the OVMM model directly -- which proves the optics, not the chip.
open_questions.blocks: ovmm_one_su outright, and gemm_oracle's bit-exact optical claim.

open_questions.question: Do nic_bridge, nic_crypto and nic_dma get a capability rung, or are they out of scope for the FMOD? They are the only T100 blocks that owe nothing to any inference rung. Today they sit on link_beat, which proves a payload crosses a link and nothing about whether the NIC path works. The likeliest answer is a NET0 loopback rung shaped like host_loopback -- see the dma-engine-rungs question below, which is the general form of this one.
open_questions.blocks: Whether three units need owners, and whether W1 is really complete.

open_questions.question:
Half answered by #256, and the half that is left is sharper for it. The DFE now dispatches to the unit directly -- dfe_fmod.hpp pushes an XPU command onto its own eu_xpu_cmd port rather than through a shared engine bus -- so "assembled but not dispatched" is no longer the problem. Two things still stop a transpose from running end to end:
G64, which the unit's README calls blocking. dfe_fmod fills each 64-byte descriptor slot with the raw 8-bit index instead of the resolved descriptor, which decodes to a zero extent, so xpu refuses it with bad_geometry. The ids and the cqid flow correctly, so what is missing is exactly DFDT resolution in the DFE -- a DFE change, not an XPU one.
And the runtime's two backends still do not know the opcode. Neither OpuEngineBus::execute nor IntrinsicsEngineBus::execute handles XPU, so a region containing a transpose faults terminally on fmod:// and on intrinsics:// alike. That path is untouched by #256.
Still worth staring at for the reason it was first written down. The unit passes 25 of 25 of its own tests: the per-unit view says it is the healthiest block on the chip, and the chip view says a transpose does not run. That gap is invisible to a per-unit test plan by construction, and it is the best argument on this ladder for ordering chip tests by minimal machinery -- one transpose is the smallest op there is, and it is the one that does not run.
open_questions.blocks: vpu_chain outright, and every rung above it.

open_questions.question:
Chapter 1.1 describes four engines with independent command streams -- DFE, HOST, NET0 and inter-OPU DMA -- and three of the four can be exercised with no compute stack at all. HOST now has host_loopback. NET0 (nic_bridge, nic_crypto, nic_dma, serdes) and inter-OPU DMA (send, opu_dma) have no chip rung, only the tile_in_tm and link_beat unit rungs. Should each get a loopback rung of the same shape as host_loopback?
Note the engine count is itself unsettled: chapter 11 lists five, having split inter-OPU DMA into local (UCIe) and remote (PCIe). Settle the count before encoding it.
open_questions.blocks: Whether five units have any chip-level obligation at all.

open_questions.question: csr_readback's unit list is maintained by hand and is known to be under-inclusive -- xpu only appeared on it because its test plan claimed the tag. Should the list be derived from which units have a register SSoT?
open_questions.blocks: Nothing yet. It will start understating the rung as units land.

bringup_strategy.label: Phoebe-first op bring-up

order.step: Add the op to the runtime, on intrinsics:// first.
order.why: Real arithmetic with no unit structure, so semantics are settled where a failure has one cause. A contract test can run here long before the FMOD can execute it, which is what the intrinsics column is for.

order.step: Adopt it in Phoebe immediately, against a tiny synthetic model.
order.why: This is the step that pays, and it is the one a contract test cannot substitute for. An op repeatedly passed its own test and then could not be reached from a real caller: the embedding gather works and needs the whole table in Tensor Memory (models#344); the kernel table freezes at first submission, so an epsilon has to be reserved before any weight upload; `mul` has no broadcast, so a bias add and a scalar scale are not expressible as written. None of those are visible from inside the runtime.

order.step: Gate on numeric parity against PyTorch, then measure the cost.
order.why: Parity on a tiny model is checkable by anyone and fails for one reason at a time. The cost measurement -- regions, opcodes, transferred bytes -- is what turns "it works" into an architectural argument: models#401 is an ISA ask backed by a region count, not by an opinion.

order.step: Close the host-side gap the adoption exposed, then port to fmod://.
order.why: Each op leaves the host doing strictly less, and what remains is a list rather than a feeling. The AMOD then has to run a program that is known to be the right program.

bringup_strategy.evidence: The sequence as actually run, each entry an op that went runtime-then-Phoebe: the OVMM surface GEMM, elementwise add/mul/gelu with device-resident chaining, RMSNorm at a model's own epsilon, softmax and RoPE, slice and write_slice, attention over a device KV cache, a decoder block's residual additions, int4 quantize/dequantize with a per-token scale derived on the device, and a sparse MoE block. Each one is a merged pair of PRs -- one in models, one in phoebe -- and the Phoebe half is where the surprises were.
bringup_strategy.what_the_fmod_inherits:
Three things, in decreasing order of confidence.
The op order. It is not arbitrary: it is the order in which a Llama forward stops needing the host, and every step was chosen because the previous one made it the cheapest remaining gap. An FMOD bring-up that follows it gets the same property, that each new rung fails for one reason.
The tests. Phoebe's suites are parity-against-PyTorch on synthetic models, which is exactly the shape a gate test wants, and several of them would port to runtime/tests/contract/ nearly unchanged. `moe_block`'s gate is unwritten for want of that port rather than for want of a design.
The measurements. Region and opcode counts taken on intrinsics are valid instruction-level facts about the program regardless of backend, so the AMOD inherits a cost baseline it did not have to generate. What it does not inherit is timing -- see the PMOD prerequisites in architecture/doc/projects/t100-ovmm-issue-granularity.md.
bringup_strategy.caveat:
Two ways this could mislead, both worth stating because the strategy is being recommended rather than merely reported.
Everything above ran on tiny synthetic models -- d_model 32, two layers, four experts. Parity there is not parity at 4096, and no amount of it substitutes for one_token on a real checkpoint.
And a capability reached on intrinsics can be reached in a way the AMOD cannot execute at all, because intrinsics computes an operation instead of walking it through the model. The UTM-only rule on VCALL operands is the example: it was added to intrinsics specifically to stop programs being written that the real machine could not run, and it broke every Phoebe program that existed at the time. Expect the port to fmod:// to find more of those, and treat an intrinsics green as evidence about the program rather than about the machine.

completion.name: completion
completion.desc: Unit -> DFE completion port: reports a retired instruction's tensor ids (src0/src1/dst descriptor indices) so the DFE can advance progress tracking (ctl_type dsync/isync, last_write/last_read counters).
completion.notes: The payload is chapter 4's `completion_token` field-for-field: three 8-bit descriptor ids, each with its own valid bit, 27 bits in the spec's bit order (src0v, src0, src1v, src1, dstv, dst). The valid bits are not decoration -- an earlier revision of this file encoded 'unused operand' as id 0, which is wrong, because descriptor 0 is a legal DFRT entry and an instruction really reading it would have looked identical to one reading nothing. Table 4.2.8 spends three bits to avoid exactly that.

parameter.desc: Tensor id / descriptor-index width (matches the ISA's src0/src1/dst fields).

clock.desc: Interface clock. All signals sampled on the rising edge.

reset.desc: Synchronous, active-low reset.

cmp.desc: Retired-instruction report: the tensor ids the completed instruction read (src0/src1) and wrote (dst), each with its valid bit. One transfer is one `completion_token` (Table 4.2.8): dst sets one Rdy bit, src0 and src1 each decrement one RdCnt.

signal.name: cqid
signal.desc: The dispatch's cqid, returned unmodified. Sets the DFCQ entry's `complete` bit, which is what lets the head pointer advance and the instruction retire in program order (4.2.8.1).

signal.name: src0v
signal.desc: src0 descriptor is valid; when clear, no decrement is performed for src0.

signal.name: src0
signal.desc: src0 descriptor id -- the DFRT entry whose RdCnt is decremented.

signal.name: src1v
signal.desc: src1 descriptor is valid; when clear, no decrement is performed for src1.

signal.name: src1
signal.desc: src1 descriptor id -- the second DFRT entry whose RdCnt is decremented.

signal.name: dstv
signal.desc: Destination descriptor is valid; when clear, no Rdy bit is set.

signal.name: dst
signal.desc: Destination descriptor id -- the DFRT entry whose Rdy bit is set, releasing every instruction waiting on it as a source.

signal.name: valid
signal.desc: Completion valid (asserted by the executing unit).

signal.name: ready
signal.desc: Completion ready (asserted by the DFE).

ssot_gap.desc: The chapter and its own generated table disagree about what a completion token contains. Prose, 4.2.8.1: 'The cqid rides through the DFSC and the execution unit and is returned with the completion token, which sets that entry's complete bit.' Table: isa/dfrt.toml types `completion_token` as exactly 27 bits -- {src0v, src0, src1v, src1, dstv, dst} -- with no cqid field. Both cannot describe the same wire. The DFCQ is what makes retirement in-order, and its complete bit is set by cqid, so a token without one cannot retire anything; a 27-bit token means the DFE would have to recover the cqid some other way, and no other way is described.
ssot_gap.assumed: The prose. This port carries the cqid alongside the 27-bit token, 35 bits of payload, on the grounds that the generated table is typing the DFRT-facing part of the token -- its own description is about setting Rdy and decrementing RdCnt, which is all the DFRT does -- and simply does not reach the DFCQ. Filed against the spec so the table and the prose converge on one answer; if the answer is that the token really is 27 bits, then the ids are also redundant with the cqid and this whole payload collapses to 8 bits.

ssot_gap.desc: No `bytes_moved` field. The performance model charges memory bandwidth on the number of bytes a transfer actually moved; without it, PMOD has to reconstruct the transfer size from the descriptor, which duplicates the engine's own address generation and will disagree with it on any partial or clipped transfer.
ssot_gap.assumed: PMOD reconstructs the size from the dispatched descriptor.

ssot_gap.desc: No `status` field, so there is no error path on the retirement port at all: a unit cannot report that an instruction retired abnormally. Related to G14 on the eu interface -- these are two ends of the same missing fault story.
ssot_gap.assumed: Every reported retirement is successful.

ssot_gap.desc: Is retirement correlated by tensor id or by an explicit tag? This port reports src0/src1/dst tensor ids, which correlates only while completion is in dispatch order; two in-flight instructions writing the same dst are indistinguishable. An explicit transaction tag would make correlation exact and is what out-of-order completion would need.
ssot_gap.assumed: Strictly oldest-first retirement, ignoring src0/src1/dst; a completion arriving with nothing in flight is counted as an orphan and dropped.

dma.desc: Host-DMA transfer descriptor and completion for host system memory <-> HBM.
dma.notes: The live host_dma model accepts only the flat byte-count shape chapter 11 defines and refuses rank, dimensions, or strides. Address-space legality is enforced by the engine and reported as illegal_space.

parameter.name: SPACE_WIDTH
parameter.desc: Address-space selector. A nibble on purpose: the tensor descriptor's `address.ast` is a 4-bit space selector, so if G20 is settled by allocating codes out of its reserved 0x2..0xF this field is already the right shape.

parameter.name: ADDR_WIDTH
parameter.desc: Endpoint byte address within its space. A full 64 bits because two of the four spaces are off-die (host sysmem, msic) and neither has a narrower envelope the model may assume.

parameter.name: STRIDE_WIDTH
parameter.desc: One per-dimension stride, in bytes, SIGNED two's complement.

parameter.name: DIM_WIDTH
parameter.desc: One per-dimension extent, in runs of `elem_bytes`. Matches the tensor descriptor's 32-bit `dims` element so a converged descriptor does not have to requantise extents.

parameter.name: MAX_DIMS
parameter.desc: Rank ceiling: the element count of `dims` and of both stride vectors. Four, matching the tensor descriptor's four `dims`. Declared for consumers sizing an array; the `count` keys below must repeat the literal because the generator takes a number there, not a parameter name.

parameter.name: RANK_WIDTH
parameter.desc: Width of `rank`. Three bits for the range 1..4, mirroring the tensor descriptor's `ndims`.

parameter.name: LEN_WIDTH
parameter.desc: Total bytes in the transfer.

parameter.name: ELEM_BYTES_WIDTH
parameter.desc: Size of the innermost contiguous run, in bytes. 32 bits: a run wider than 4 GiB is not a transfer any of these engines issues, and narrowing it would invent a constraint nobody has stated.

parameter.name: TAG_WIDTH
parameter.desc: Host-DMA transfer tag, echoed on completion. The width is provisional until the host SQ-to-DMA correlation format is specified; see G91.

parameter.name: SIGNAL_ID_WIDTH
parameter.desc: Host fence-bank index. The width is provisional until the SQ-to-fence mapping is specified; see G91.

parameter.name: BYTE_COUNT_WIDTH
parameter.desc: Bytes actually moved by a completed transfer. The performance model charges memory bandwidth on this.

ssot_gap.desc: Can the architecture's tensor descriptor describe a strided transfer? RFC-T100-0005 §6 defines `RASTER` as "affine, full per-dim stride generality", but the 64-byte descriptor carries `dims` and `tdims` and no stride fields. With only extents, a stride can only be the product of the extents nested inside it, so every tensor that descriptor describes is necessarily densely packed and a strided view -- a slice of a larger tensor, a row pitch wider than the row -- is not representable at all. That is a real capability and not a hypothetical: this port puts strides on the ENDPOINT precisely so the two sides can differ, and the tdma tests exercise it. Either §6 overstates what `RASTER` can express, or the descriptor is missing a stride vector.
ssot_gap.assumed: The strided capability survives on this transfer descriptor, whose `src_strides` and `dst_strides` are the per-dimension stride vector the tensor descriptor lacks; `tdma`, which did adopt the tensor descriptor, is dense-only until this is settled. So the model carries two descriptor shapes, which is the duplication converging on one was meant to remove.

ssot_gap.desc: How does the architecture name a `host` or `msic` endpoint? The tensor descriptor's `address.ast` is a 4-bit space selector defining exactly `0x0 = HBM` and `0x1 = UTM`, with `0x2..0xF` reserved (MBZ). This port's spaces are { tm, hbm, host, remote_hbm, nic, msic } -- four of the six have no encoding, and `host` is the one that matters here, because `host_dma` exists to move host <-> HBM. (`msic` is now unclaimed on this port: SEND reaches the MS buffers over `ms_buf`.) The tensor descriptor therefore cannot describe what either engine does, and allocating codes out of the reserved range (or stating that non-tensor endpoints deliberately belong to a sibling transfer descriptor) is the precondition for one descriptor across all three DMA engines.
ssot_gap.assumed: This interface defines its own 4-bit `AddrSpace` with all six codes, and only `tdma` -- which moves tensors HBM <-> TM and so is genuinely describable -- consumes the tensor descriptor. The nibble is deliberately the same width as `ast` so these codes can move into it unchanged once the reserved range is allocated.

ssot_gap.desc: Half this descriptor is not a host DMA transfer. Chapter 11 defines the host engine's request as the SQ `DMA` packet -- {engine, dir, slot, dma_flags, len_bytes, src_addr, dst_addr} -- and then rules layout out explicitly, twice: 11.1, 'len_bytes is a byte count. Layout conversion/transpose is described by TDesc.layout / DSFC and is not a DMA transport field'; 11.3.1, 'The DMA payload has no generic ctx field. Tensor layout/transpose is described by TDesc.layout / DSFC in the memory model, not the transport command.' So for host_dma, `rank`, `dims`, both stride vectors and `elem_bytes` describe something the architecture says this engine does not do -- eleven of the descriptor's fields against the seven the chapter names. Chapter 11 also has no `slot`, and `dma_flags` is reserved, so the mapping between the two shapes is not merely a subset.
ssot_gap.assumed: host_dma executes the flat case only: rank <= 1, both stride vectors all-zero, and len as the byte count. A descriptor asking for anything else is refused with bad_stride and counted. The narrow fix is to drop the unused layout fields; the wide one is G20, since host_dma needs a descriptor that can name a host endpoint.

ssot_gap.desc: What are the host SQ-to-DMA tag and fence-id widths? Chapter 11 defines queue slots, completion entries, and fence behavior but does not define this internal transfer port. TAG_WIDTH=32 and SIGNAL_ID_WIDTH=16 therefore have no architectural source.
ssot_gap.assumed: Keep the current 32-bit transfer tag and 16-bit fence id until the host interface specifies the internal correlation format. This port is host-driven and does not share the DFE completion channel's cqid.

eu.name: eu
eu.desc: DFE -> execution-unit dispatch port (one instance per unit): carries a decoded compute instruction (OVMM, VCALL or XPU) with its resolved operand/destination descriptors, the identity it must quote back on completion, and, for VCALL, the VPU kernel entry address.
eu.notes: Opcodes and field widths follow ssot/isa/dfe_isa.toml. vpu_kernel_addr widens the instruction's 29-bit pc_addr field (VPU kernel PC HBM address) to a resolved 64-bit byte address; it is meaningful only when op=VCALL and zero otherwise. ctl_type sync semantics (msync for OVMM, dsync/isync) are enforced by the DFE dispatcher before issue and do not travel on this port. The cqid and the three descriptor ids are here because the completion port needs them and cannot invent them: 4.2.8.1 has the cqid 'ride through the DFSC and the execution unit', and Table 4.2.8 builds the completion token out of the three ids, so a unit that received only resolved descriptors could not answer. Sending the resolved descriptor AND its id is not redundancy in the model's favour -- the descriptor is what the work needs and the id is what the bookkeeping needs, and they are read by different parts of the unit.

parameter.name: DESC_WIDTH
parameter.desc: Descriptor payload width: one tensor descriptor. Sized from the descriptor spec rather than typed here -- it moved from 32 to 64 bytes upstream and the hand-typed 256 did not follow.

parameter.name: KADDR_WIDTH
parameter.desc: VPU kernel entry-address width (resolved HBM byte address).

parameter.name: TID_WIDTH
parameter.desc: Descriptor-index width, matching the ISA's src0/src1/dst fields and the completion port's ids.

parameter.name: CQID_WIDTH
parameter.desc: Completion-queue id width. 4.2.8.1: 'an 8-bit completion id (cqid[7:0], plus a wrap bit for full/empty detection)'. The wrap bit stays inside the DFE -- it distinguishes full from empty on the pointers, which is not something a unit can observe or needs to.
